author: EmuCore - Hub
title: PS2 Mouse Kernel Development Tutorial
summary: Dragon Zap Education uses PlayStation 2 mouse support as a compact kernel-development lesson, connecting a concrete input device to a wider multithreaded operating-system course instead of presenting it as an emulator controller menu.

blocks.text: Across ten focused minutes, the tutorial treats the mouse beneath the application layer. Because it belongs to a course on building a multithreaded kernel from scratch, the PS2 target becomes an example of device discovery, data delivery and coordination with code that cannot assume a desktop operating system is already present. A visible cursor or event is only the final proof; the educational interest is the path between hardware input and a consumer task. The linked course module provides the surrounding sequence for viewers who need prerequisites.

The public description contains only a discounted course link and does not identify source code, PS/2 electrical interface details, controller commands, interrupt route, buffer design, synchronization primitive or test hardware. “PS2” in the title refers to the PlayStation 2 context selected by the catalogue, but viewers should verify terminology inside the video because PS/2 also names a keyboard-and-mouse port standard. Do not infer a console-wide driver from the title alone. Use the lesson as a kernel concept entry and require code-level documentation before replication.
